subStrands.name: African and Non-African Prose Set Texts

objectives.description: African Prose: appreciation of plot, character, theme, setting, style and language in African prose set texts (e.g. Second Class Citizen by Buchi Emecheta; Unexpected Joy at Dawn by Alex Agyei-Agyiri).
Non-African Prose: appreciation of plot, character, theme, setting, style and language in non-African prose set texts (e.g. Invisible Man by Ralph Ellison; Wuthering Heights by Emily Brontë).
African Drama: appreciation of dramatic techniques, themes, characterisation and language in African drama set texts (e.g. Let Me Die Alone by John K. Kargbo; The Lion and the Jewel by Wole Soyinka).
Shakespearean Text: appreciation of dramatic structure, language, themes and characterisation in a Shakespeare play (e.g. A Midsummer Night's Dream).
Non-African Drama: appreciation of dramatic techniques, themes and language in non-African drama set texts (e.g. Look Back in Anger by John Osborne; Fences by August Wilson).

African Poetry: appreciation of imagery, diction, tone, mood, theme and poetic devices in African poetry set texts (e.g. 'Black Woman' by Léopold Sédar Senghor; 'The Leader and the Led' by Niyi Osundare; 'The Song of the Women of my Land' by Oumar Farouk Sesay; 'Raider of the Treasure Trove' by Lade Wosornu; 'A Government Driver on his Retirement' by Onu Chibuike).

Non-African Poetry: appreciation of imagery, diction, tone, mood, theme and poetic devices in non-African poetry set texts (e.g. 'The Good-Morrow' by John Donne; 'Caged Bird' by Maya Angelou; 'The Journey of the Magi' by T.S. Eliot; 'Do not Go Gentle into the Good Night' by Dylan Thomas; 'Binsey Poplars' by G.M. Hopkins; 'Bat' by D.H. Lawrence).
Basic principles of literary appreciation: meaning of literature; genres (prose, poetry, drama); literary terms and devices; themes, plot, character, setting, style and language.
Oral literature: characteristics and forms of oral literature (myths, legends, folktales, proverbs, riddles, dirges, praise poetry); functions of oral literature in society.
